classification.difficultyReason: Use equal base angles and the triangle angle sum in differently oriented isosceles triangles.

content.prompt:
Use the angle sum of a triangle to find the value of the pronumeral in these isosceles triangles.
You do not need to show working out.

spec.description: Upright unshaded triangle with horizontal base, double ticks on both sloping sides, a° at lower left and 68° at lower right.
spec.mathematics: The marked equal sides imply equal base angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown label are visible.

answer.worked:
Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.
$$a=68^\circ$$

spec.description: Oblique triangle with left, lower-right and upper-right vertices. Double ticks mark the two sides meeting at lower right. The left angle is 37° and the lower-right angle is a°.
spec.mathematics: The upper-right angle equals 37°; the lower-right vertex angle completes the triangle angle sum.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown label are visible.

answer.worked:
The other base angle is $37^\circ$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle).
$$\begin{align*}a+37+37&=180 &&\text{(angle sum of triangle)}\\a+74&=180\\a&=106^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Right-pointing unshaded triangle with vertical left side. Double ticks mark the two sides meeting at the right vertex. The lower-left angle is 80° and the right angle is a°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown label are visible.

answer.worked:
The other base angle is $80^\circ$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle).
$$\begin{align*}a+80+80&=180 &&\text{(angle sum of triangle)}\\a+160&=180\\a&=20^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upright unshaded triangle with horizontal base, double ticks on the sloping sides, 50° at the top and a° at lower left.
spec.mathematics: The two base angles are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown label are visible.

answer.worked:
The other base angle is $a^\circ$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle).
$$\begin{align*}a+a+50&=180 &&\text{(angle sum of triangle)}\\2a+50&=180\\2a&=130\\a&=65^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Tall oblique triangle with top, lower-left and right vertices. Double ticks mark the two sides meeting at right. The right angle is 100° and the top angle is a°.
spec.mathematics: The top and lower-left base angles are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown label are visible.

answer.worked:
The other base angle is $a^\circ$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle).
$$\begin{align*}a+a+100&=180 &&\text{(angle sum of triangle)}\\2a+100&=180\\2a&=80\\a&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Tall oblique triangle with upper-left, upper-right and bottom vertices. Double ticks mark the two sides meeting at bottom. The bottom angle is 28° and the upper-left angle is a°.
spec.mathematics: The upper-left and upper-right base angles are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown label are visible.

answer.worked:
The other base angle is $a^\circ$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle).
$$\begin{align*}a+a+28&=180 &&\text{(angle sum of triangle)}\\2a+28&=180\\2a&=152\\a&=76^\circ\end{align*}$$
